title: SCE observation trace (wire schema v1)
description: What an engine driver observed when it ran the scenarios of a scenario set against one design: for every step of every scenario, the events the machine sent outward, whether it had finished, which states were active, and the data it could read. Written by a driver, a program separate from SCE, and read by `sce-codegen judge-scenarios`, which compares it with what the scenarios expect. A driver declares in `observes` which of those it can see at all, because a scenario that asks about something the driver cannot see is not judged, which is not the same as failing it. A trace says nothing about whether a design is right: it is the record the judgement is made from. Authoritative reader is sce-build/src/scenario_judge.rs. The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone — see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md.

name.description: A name from the scenario set or the design: an event, a state, a data item.

scalar.description: A value a payload field or a data item holds.

channel.description: `true` when the driver observes this channel, or `{"unavailable": why}` when it cannot, with the reason a scenario asking about it will be told.

sent.description: An event the machine sent to something outside itself.

observation.description: What was seen at the end of one step. Each key is present exactly when its channel is observed: `outbound` lists what was sent outward DURING the step (empty when nothing was), `finished` is the state after, `configuration` is every active state id with its ancestors, `data` holds the names the driver could read.

run.description: One scenario. Either `observations`, one per step of the scenario in order, or `refused`, why the driver did not run it (an event the design has no transition for, a design the driver could not build).

record.description: Names this file as an observation trace, so a file of another kind is refused rather than half read.

v.description: The wire version of this record. A file of another version is refused.

engine.description: Who drove the machine. Repeated in every judgement, because a verdict is about an engine: the same examples can pass on one runtime and fail on another.

design.description: The design that was driven, as the driver names it. Informational: the judge does not read the design.

scenario_set.description: The scenario set the driver ran, by digest. When given and different from the set being judged, nothing is judged.

observes.description: Which channels this driver can see at all.

unreadable.description: Data names the driver knows it cannot read, each with why (a generator that gave the item no reader, say). A name missing from an observation's `data` is a gap either way; this is what lets the gap say why.
